info.title: Hermes Native Client API
info.description: The stable, authenticated API exposed by the Next.js host to native clients. Hermes itself remains loopback-only and this server remains the sole consumer of Hermes run streams.

get.summary: Replay then follow project events over SSE
get.description: Each run event has an SSE id of runId:sequence. Reconnect with Last-Event-ID or cursor. Sequence numbers are scoped to a run; when the resolved run changes, the server replays it from -1. The stream closes after a terminal run event and clients reconnect with backoff.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Fallback for clients that cannot set Last-Event-ID.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Explicit run returned by POST messages.

200.description: SSE frames. Keepalives are comments and have no id.

post.summary: Run a Hermes slash command in this session
post.description: Carried out by the gateway itself (`slash.exec` under session authority), not by the model. The gateway decides which commands it runs; a refusal is 409 with its reason in the message. `exec` returns the command's Markdown output, which is not written to the transcript. `send` means the command rewrote itself into a prompt: submit `message` as an ordinary message to run it. 503 when the gateway cannot be reached or does not run commands for other clients — see GET /api/v1/commands.

post.summary: Respond to a pending approval

get.summary: Read a run and what it is blocked on
get.description: The host's own record of the run, which outlives Hermes' (a terminal run is forgotten upstream after an hour). `pending_approval` and `pending_question` are set only while the status is `waiting_for_approval`.

post.summary: Answer a question the agent asked mid-run
post.description: Answers the pending `clarify.request` on this run. The host supplies the prompt id and execution generation the gateway requires. 409 when nothing is pending — already answered elsewhere, timed out, or the run moved on. Only gateways under session authority ask these.

post.summary: Acknowledge a run Hermes lost the owner of
post.description: A run whose owner died mid-turn is neither finished nor running, and later turns in its session wait behind it. The host settles such a run as `run.failed` with `unknown: true` in the payload; this acknowledges it upstream so the chat can continue. Requires `features.run_unknown_resolution` on the gateway. 409 when Hermes does not report the run as unknown.

get.description: Probes the gateway's control socket on the host. `?bot=<profile>` asks for a Bot's profile. Clients should offer gateway-run commands only when `available` is true.

activeSessionId.description: Server fallback session for cold starts and legacy routes; not a cross-device UI selection.

scheduledSessionId.description: Set on the General project only: its single chat, where every bound scheduled job reports. It is an ordinary chat (kind "chat"); reply to reports with a normal message. General refuses new chats and branches with 409 general_single_chat.

unreadScheduledCount.description: Unread reports in the General chat; 0 for every other project.

bot.description: The Hermes profile (Bot Mode Bot) this project runs as, fixed at creation; null is the default profile. Absent from servers that predate Bot Mode support.

id.description: Canonical profile id; "default" for the gateway's own profile.

name.description: The Bot's display name, which stands in for the agent's name in this project.

bot.description: Bind the new project to this Hermes profile id. Cannot be changed later.

botChat.description: With bot: open the Bot's canonical Bot Chat rather than a new session. 409 when another project already holds it.

kind.description: Always "chat" from current servers. "scheduled" was the retired per-project Scheduled inbox and is kept in the enum for older servers.

botChat.description: True on a Bot's canonical "Bot Chat": never renamed upstream and not deletable through this API. Absent from servers that predate Bot Mode support.

activeSessionId.description: Session returned by this operation when applicable.
Server fallback session for cold starts and legacy routes; not a cross-device UI selection.

content_format.description: How clients should render content. Generated assistant and cron output is Markdown; user, system, and tool content is plain text.

mode.description: `steered` means the text went into the run in flight: injected with steer, or — when the run is blocked on a `clarify.request` — taken as its answer (text without attachments, `prefer` not `queue`).

answer.description: Free text, or one of the offered choices. For a multi-select, the JSON-encoded array of picked choices.

command.description: The whole line, leading slash included, e.g. `/usage` or `/goal ship the release`.

output.description: Markdown, as the gateway writes it for messaging platforms.

reason.description: Why not, as a code: control_unreachable, not_ready, session_authority_unavailable, profile_mismatch, unsafe_control_peer, …

type.description: message.delta, message.interim, tool.started, tool.completed, reasoning.available, subagent.start, subagent.complete, approval.request, approval.responded, clarify.request, clarify.settled, run.queued, run.steered, run.stopping, run.completed, run.failed, run.cancelled, or a project event. A gateway shutdown mid-run arrives as run.failed with `interrupted: true`; a run whose owner was lost as run.failed with `unknown: true`. Clients must ignore types they do not know.

runActive.description: Whether the referenced run is currently active; null for project events without a run

JobBinding.description: Present when the job reports to this app. Every binding reports into the General chat: on write, any non-empty project_id binds and its value is ignored; on read, project_id is the General project.

health_detailed.description: GET /health/detailed from the gateway; null when it has no such route.
